definitions.definition: to make a continuous low sound:
definitions.example: The computers were humming in the background.

definitions.definition: to sing without opening your mouth:
definitions.example: She hummed to herself as she walked to school.

definitions.definition: to make a continuous, low sound, or to sing a tune with closed lips:
definitions.example: Debbie always hums to herself when she listens to music.

definitions.definition: a continuous low noise:
definitions.example: Our house is on a main street, so we can hear the constant hum of traffic.

definitions.definition: being, relating to, or belonging to a person or to people as opposed to animals:
definitions.example: The human body is composed of about 60 percent water.

definitions.definition: having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines:
definitions.example: Of course I make mistakes, I'm only human.

definitions.definition: of or typical of people:
definitions.example: the human body

definitions.definition: relating to people:
definitions.example: Most of the problems were caused by human error, poor communication and staffing issues.

definitions.definition: a member of a species of the genus (= group of species)Homo:
definitions.example: Extinct species of the genus (collectively called archaic humans) include H. habilis, H. erectus, and H. neanderthalensis.

definitions.definition: (a person who is) involved in or connected with improving people's lives and reducing suffering:
definitions.example: The prisoner has been released for humanitarian reasons.

definitions.definition: understanding and kindness toward other people:
definitions.example: If only he would show a little humanity for once.

definitions.definition: not proud or not believing that you are important:
definitions.example: He's very humble about his success.

definitions.definition: ordinary; not special or very important:
definitions.example: At that time she was just a humble mechanic.

definitions.definition: to make someone understand that they are not as important or special as they thought:
definitions.example: He was humbled by the child's generosity.

definitions.definition: (of air and weather conditions) containing extremely small drops of water in the air:
definitions.example: New York is very hot and humid in the summer.

definitions.definition: to make someone feel ashamed or lose respect for himself or herself:
definitions.example: How could you humiliate me by questioning my judgment in front of everyone like that?

definitions.definition: the feeling of being ashamed or losing respect for yourself, or an occasion when you have this feeling:
definitions.example: After the humiliation of last week's defeat, the Mets were back on in form.

definitions.definition: an idea that is based on feeling and for which there is no proof:
definitions.example: I had a hunch that you'd be here.

definitions.definition: to lean forward with your shoulders raised or to bend your back and shoulders into a rounded shape:
definitions.example: We hunched around the fire to keep warm.

definitions.definition: the number 100:
definitions.example: We've driven a/one hundred miles in the last two hours.
We’ve driven a/one hundred miles in the last two hours.

definitions.definition: the feeling you have when you need to eat:
definitions.example: I can't believe that that enormous meal wasn't enough to satisfy your hunger.

definitions.definition: wanting or needing food:
definitions.example: By four o'clock I was really hungry.

definitions.definition: having a strong wish or desire for something:
definitions.example: She was so hungry for success that she'd do anything to achieve it.

definitions.definition: feeling the need to eat because there has been a period of time when you have not eaten:
definitions.example: The children are always hungry when they get home from school.

definitions.definition: having a great need or wish for something:
definitions.example: Analysts said investors were hungry for any information that could point the market in a direction.

definitions.definition: having a great need or wish for the stated thing:
definitions.example: capital-/cash-/money-hungry

definitions.definition: to chase and try to catch and kill an animal or bird for food, sport, or profit:
definitions.example: Some animals hunt at night.

definitions.definition: to try to find something or someone:
definitions.example: I've hunted all over the place, but I can't find that book.

definitions.definition: to chase or search for a wild animal or bird with the intention of killing or catching it for food, sport, or profit:
definitions.example: He hunts every weekend.

definitions.definition: a search for something or someone:
definitions.example: After a long hunt we finally found a house we liked.

definitions.definition: someone who is trying to find or get the stated thing:
definitions.example: a job-hunter

definitions.definition: a frame or fence for jumping over in a race:
definitions.example: He fell at the last hurdle.

definitions.definition: a problem that you have to deal with before you can make progress:
definitions.example: Getting a work permit was the first hurdle to overcome.

definitions.definition: a problem that you must solve or deal with before you can make progress:
definitions.example: The first hurdle she faced entering the job market was one of confidence.

definitions.definition: to throw something with a lot of force, usually in an angry or violent way:
definitions.example: In a fit of temper he hurled the book across the room.

definitions.definition: to throw something forcefully:
definitions.example: The volcano hurled hundreds of tons of rock, ash, and dust into the air.

definitions.definition: a stick with a wide, flat oval end, used in the sport of hurling (= an Irish team game similar to field hockey):
definitions.example: He flicked the ball up with his hurl and hit it goalwards.

definitions.definition: a violent wind that has a circular movement, especially in the West Atlantic Ocean:
definitions.example: The state of Florida was hit by a hurricane that did serious damage.

definitions.definition: to move or do things more quickly than normal or to make someone do this:
definitions.example: Hurry or you'll be late.

definitions.definition: to move or act quickly, or to cause someone to move or act quickly:
definitions.example: We have to hurry if we’re going to make it there in time.

definitions.definition: the need to move or do things more quickly than normal:
definitions.example: We left in such a hurry that we forgot our tickets.

definitions.definition: the need to move or act more quickly than normal:
definitions.example: We’ve got plenty of time – what’s the hurry (= Why hurry)?

definitions.definition: to feel pain in a part of your body, or to injure someone or cause them pain:
definitions.example: Tell me where it hurts.

definitions.definition: to cause emotional pain to someone:
definitions.example: She criticized my writing quite severely and that hurt.

definitions.definition: to cause harm or difficulty:
definitions.example: A lot of businesses are being hurt by the current high interest rates.

definitions.definition: to feel pain, or to cause pain or injury to yourself or someone else:
definitions.example: Tell me where it hurts.

definitions.definition: To hurt also means to cause harm or difficulty:
definitions.example: A lot of businesses are being hurt by high interest rates.

definitions.definition: injured or in pain:
definitions.example: Let me help you up. Are you hurt?

definitions.definition: upset or unhappy:
definitions.example: I feel very hurt by what you said.

definitions.definition: feeling pain or being upset:
definitions.example: I saw you fall – are you hurt?

definitions.definition: emotional pain:
definitions.example: The hurt after a relationship breaks up can be awful.

definitions.definition: a small, simple building, usually consisting of one room:
definitions.example: a mountain hut

definitions.definition: used in football as a signal to start playing:
definitions.example: It could be that "hike" evolved into "hut" because of football's love of military terminology.

definitions.definition: a plant or animal that has been produced from two different types of plant or animal, especially to get better characteristics:
definitions.example: The garden strawberry is a large-fruited hybrid.

definitions.definition: a bicycle that has a mixture of features of different specialized bicycles, so that it works well in a range of conditions:
definitions.example: You can rent hybrids, racers, or mountain bikes.

definitions.definition: something that is a combination of two different things, so it has qualities relating to both of them:
definitions.example: a hybrid car/vehicle/engine

definitions.definition: used to describe a vehicle with an engine that uses both gas and another type of energy, usually electricity:
definitions.example: A hybrid car could save you hundreds of dollars at the gas pump.

definitions.definition: used to describe a way of working that involves sometimes being physically present and sometimes working at a distance using the internet:
definitions.example: Hybrid teaching combines traditional in-class teaching with online teaching.

definitions.definition: the degree to which people keep themselves or their environment clean, especially to prevent disease:
definitions.example: Poor standards of hygiene mean that the disease spreads fast.

definitions.definition: care and attention that is given to keeping yourself and your environment clean, especially to prevent disease:
definitions.example: Hospital staff blamed the spread of infections on poor hygiene.

definitions.definition: a situation in which something is advertised and discussed in newspapers, on television, etc. a lot in order to attract everyone's interest:
definitions.example: media hype

definitions.definition: advertising, news reports, and public praise for a new product or service, which is used to make people excited about buying or trying it:
definitions.example: marketing/advertising/media hype

definitions.definition: to advertise or praise something a lot in newspapers, on television, online, etc. in order to make people excited about it and want to buy or try it:
definitions.example: Over-enthusiastic followers hyped this company to the moon and now sales are failing to match those heady expectations.

definitions.definition: unable to control your feelings or behavior because you are extremely frightened, angry, excited, etc.:
definitions.example: Calm down, you're getting hysterical.

definitions.definition: unable to control your emotions or behavior because you are very frightened, excited, etc.:
definitions.example: Calm down, you’re getting hysterical.
